# LehmerSplit — Lehmer's even split

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: new, not yet proved

If one wheel leaves remainder 1 on division by a chosen number of intervals, the survivors of the cycle split evenly across that many equal intervals (endpoints rounded down). With wheels 2 and 3 frozen, each column splits evenly when a wheel leaves remainder 1 on division by the least common multiple of 6 and the number of intervals. UniformSubdivision's whole-count claim is the case of the rotating prime minus one intervals.

## Planned

**Will rest on:** no other node

**Planned claims:** `lehmer_even_split`, `lehmer_even_split_column`

**Evidence so far:** Both checked numerically on 4,761 cases (wheel sets from the primes up to 19, up to 24 intervals).

**Scope:** Tier 1: elementary.

**Cited by:** [`GermainCriterion`](GermainCriterion.md)

- Source: [D. H. Lehmer, The distribution of totatives, Canad. J. Math. 7 (1955), 347-357](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/A1B6054448396406512E4ECE51DC6ADD/S0008414X00030467a.pdf/distribution_of_totatives.pdf) — Theorem 4 is the whole-count form
